report:
Reviewed the complete parse.dependencies claim and all nine ordinary implementation associations plus its single explicit TODO test. The requirement is a dependency envelope: module parsing can read source, scope, edition, compilation configuration and generated parse source, but must not demand resolved names, checked interfaces, other items' semantic bodies or trait results. The permitted inputs are permissions, not requirements that every parse always read every input.

The local_syms/mods.rs association reaches the tracked unexpanded_items query, which reads module.body_source and the selected file text and passes a module scope plus ParseSource to parse_str_to_cst. Inline modules receive syntax through specify from their containing parser. parse/mod.rs builds tree-sitter syntax exclusively from supplied text and dispatches syntax construction. parse/attrs.rs reads only Configuration.cfgs in addition to syntax; cfg predicate evaluation is string/boolean processing, including unknown and malformed predicates remaining syntax. parse/items.rs constructs local identities and CST for functions, structs, enums, traits, impls, constants, statics, aliases, imports and macros. Reading bodies here means reading the current source's syntax, not demanding another item's checked body. Module handling uses scope ancestry and edition, source path/inline-directory provenance, and source-file lookup; the captured scope helper only walks parent scope identities and the concrete database source_file implementation only returns a registered source input. It does not resolve semantic names. The captured SourceFile and Configuration definitions establish these as source/config inputs.

The remaining five helper associations cover exprs, generics, paths, types and util: they recursively transform tree-sitter nodes, allocate CST/stash structures and intern text Names; none calls resolution, signature checking, body checking or trait evaluation. Path parsing retains symbolic syntax rather than resolving it. Name is a captured Salsa interned string. Utility and token extraction helpers use input text and spans. Generated macro output is passed as text and ParseSource by parse_output; expansion obtains that source before entering parse_str_to_cst, and semantic expansion resolution is not called by the parser. Inspection of all parser helpers and the module entry shows no forbidden semantic-query demand. Added associations ensure future changes to the tracked module-query file and each parser helper invalidate this assessment.

The complete test set is sage_meta::todo::modules_parse_dependencies. It intentionally has no assertions and is not evidence of runtime verification. Its explicit deferred matrix calls for a cold trace containing only allowed inputs, a warm request doing no parse work, and reuse after semantic-only edits. This is an honest test deferral: completing it requires a parse dependency/execution observation fixture spanning cold, warm, and semantic-edit revisions, with forbidden resolved-name/interface/other-body/trait demand assertions; it must also exercise configuration and generated source branches. I accept that documented TODO as deferred, without claiming these scenarios have been verified. There are no N/A entries and no production TODO associations. A future accidental signature/trait request in a parse helper would violate the claim and is not currently protected by this placeholder.

Commands actually executed: cargo meta review start/read (including a fresh start after comment changes), cargo fmt, cargo build (passed with existing warnings), and cargo test -p sage-meta --test semantic_spec modules_parse_dependencies -- --exact todo::modules_parse_dependencies (one placeholder passed). Test execution does not add substantive adequacy. Source inspection supports the implementation boundary, while cold/warm/edit behavioral verification remains explicitly TODO. The coordinator handles the delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks for the comment-only association changes.
